issues.description: validate_conda hardcodes *.exe filter — breaks the entire feature on Linux and macOS
issues.detail: The confpage passes filters='*.exe' to create_browsefile. On Linux and macOS, conda/mamba/micromamba executables have no extension. The file picker will refuse to show valid executables on the platforms where most kernel/conda users actually live. This is the kind of thing where the patch ran on the author's Windows box and nobody tried it elsewhere. Either drop the filter or branch on sys.platform.

issues.description: validate_conda returns True for empty string — silently accepts an unconfigured custom executable
issues.detail: validate_conda("") returns True. Combined with the kernelspec logic, if the user ticks 'custom_conda' but never sets a path, the validator says fine, the kernelspec then sees a falsy conda_exe and falls through to the not-found error. That's a confusing UX: the preferences page says the value is valid, the kernel says conda isn't found. Either return False on empty (forcing the user to fill it in) or gate the checkbox on a non-empty path. Don't lie in the validator.

issues.description: Substring match on '--version' output will accept anything containing 'conda' or 'mamba'
issues.detail: any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ["micromamba", "mamba", "conda"]) is a substring test against arbitrary stdout. A binary named /usr/local/bin/condarc-helper, or a script that prints 'this is not conda', will pass. The check should at minimum match the start of the version string or use a regex anchored to a version number. Also: out.decode() with no encoding argument can raise UnicodeDecodeError on a misbehaving binary, which the bare except will swallow as False — fine, but worth knowing.

issues.description: os.access(..., os.X_OK) is unreliable and meaningless on Windows
issues.detail: On Windows os.access with X_OK essentially checks for existence. On POSIX it can lie under ACLs, NFS, and setuid. The real check is the one below: try to run it and see what comes back. The X_OK gate just adds a code path that does nothing useful on Windows and can falsely reject on some POSIX configurations. Drop it; the run_program call is the actual validator.

issues.description: Two unrelated changes folded into one patch
issues.detail: edit.setFocus() in create_browsefile.select_file is a behavior change to a shared widget helper unrelated to the custom-conda feature. It will affect every browsefile picker in Spyder. That belongs in its own patch with its own justification, not snuck in at the bottom of a feature PR. THREE-PATCHES: the config plumbing, the kernelspec fallback, and the widget focus tweak should not land as one diff.

issues.description: No tests for validate_conda or the kernelspec fallback path
issues.detail: validate_conda is a pure function with clear branches (empty, missing file, non-executable, wrong tool, right tool) and is trivially testable. The kernelspec fallback (custom_conda enabled vs disabled, conda_path set vs empty) is the whole point of the PR. Neither is exercised by a test in this diff. For a feature whose failure mode is 'kernels won't start', that's thin.

issues.description: Nested ternary in kernelspec.argv is harder to read than the equivalent if-block
issues.detail: The replacement uses a ternary that spans seven lines with a nested get_conf as the condition. The surrounding code is straightforward imperative Python; this stands out. A three-line if-block reads better and matches the file's voice. Minor — but readability of the fallback is the whole point of touching this site.

review.summary: The feature is reasonable and the kernelspec fallback shape is correct: try discovery, then try the user-configured path, then error with a pointer to the new preference. NEEDS-WORK on three concrete items: the *.exe filter breaks the picker on Linux/macOS, validate_conda returning True for the empty string is a UX lie, and the substring match in validate_conda is too loose. The unrelated setFocus() change in the shared browsefile helper should be its own patch — THREE-PATCHES. No tests for the new validator or the fallback path. Fix the filter, tighten the validator (empty-string semantics and a less-permissive version check), split out the focus change, and this lands.
